title: The Three Horns
blurb: A giant fossil horn arrives at the Den. Finn and Zeb go back in time to find out what the horns were for.
cover_prompt: Finn and Zeb stand heroically at dawn on a misty prehistoric plain beside the glowing round time gate, with a huge gentle Triceratops behind them showing its two long brow horns, short nose horn and big bony frill, ferns all around and a storm cloud far away.

sound.label: /or/
sound.intro: Listen for the /or/ sound, as in horn. In this story it is spelt three ways. Tap a word to hear it.

cracked: The horns were for showing off and for pushing contests. Finn and Zeb cracked the case!

text: Finn and Zeb are in the Den. Ping!
A fossil horn has come in. It is huge!
p1.prompt: Inside the cosy explorer den full of maps and fossils, a delivery crate has just been opened on the floor, revealing a huge curved fossil horn as long as Zeb is tall; Finn kneels beside it amazed while Zeb stands next to it to compare his height, a wall screen flashing behind them.

text: What was the horn for? Nobody is sure.
Time to go back and see. Let's go!
p2.prompt: Finn and Zeb in the explorer den look up at a big wall screen showing an outline of a three-horned dinosaur skull with a big question mark symbol; Finn holds his notebook and pencil, Zeb puts on his explorer hat, ready to go.

text: They put on the time packs. The gate hums.
Zoom! They step out at dawn.
p3.prompt: Finn and Zeb, wearing small silver backpacks with glowing blue dials, step out of the glowing round time gate onto a misty prehistoric plain at dawn, the sky pink and gold, giant ferns and tall cycad plants around them.

text: It is cool and misty. Ferns drip.
Then they hear a snort, and a stomp.
p4.prompt: In a cool misty prehistoric forest of dripping ferns at dawn, Finn and Zeb freeze and cup their ears, listening, eyes wide; in the mist behind the ferns the shadow of a huge horned dinosaur head can just be seen.

text: Big prints go north, and small prints
go to the shore. Which way, Finn?
c1.prompt: On a muddy prehistoric plain, a trail of huge round dinosaur footprints leads away towards distant hills, and a trail of small round footprints leads down to a misty lake shore; Finn and Zeb stand where the trails part, Finn pointing at the big prints, Zeb pointing at the small ones.

text: The big prints go past torn ferns.
Crunch! Something big is munching.
b1a.prompt: Finn and Zeb tiptoe along a trail of huge round dinosaur footprints past ferns that have been torn and nibbled; Zeb holds up a chewed fern stem, Finn cups his ear towards a loud crunching sound behind a big rock.

text: Small prints lead to the shore.
A baby splashes, then trots off!
b1b.prompt: At a misty lake shore, a small baby Triceratops with tiny stubby horns splashes happily in the shallow water, then trots off; Finn and Zeb watch from behind reeds, smiling, following its little footprints.

text: Finn and Zeb peek round a rock. Wow!
A Triceratops! It has three horns.
p5.prompt: Finn and Zeb peek around a big mossy rock and see a huge gentle Triceratops eating ferns in a clearing, as long as a bus, with two long horns above its eyes, a short horn on its nose and a big bony frill; the boys look amazed and delighted.

text: Two long horns stick out over its eyes,
and a short one is on its nose.
p6.prompt: Close view of the gentle Triceratops' head from the side, clearly showing its two long brow horns above the eyes and the one short horn on its nose; Finn crouches nearby pointing at the horns while Zeb counts on his fingers, one, two, three.

text: It has a big bony frill and a beak like
a parrot. It nibbles more ferns.
p7.prompt: The Triceratops nibbles a leafy fern with its hooked parrot-like beak, its big bony frill fanned out behind its head, a few ferns in its mouth; Finn sketches it in his notebook, Zeb copies the beak shape with his hands, giggling.

text: Then a second one stomps up. They lower
their horns and push. Snort! Shove!
p8.prompt: Two big Triceratops face each other in a clearing and gently lock their long horns together, pushing head to head like two stags in a contest, mud flying from their feet; Finn and Zeb watch from a safe distance behind a fallen log, amazed. Nobody is hurt; it looks like a shoving game.

text: It is not a fight. It is a test of force.
Then one gets bored and trots off.
p9.prompt: One Triceratops unhooks its horns and trots away looking bored while the other stands proudly with its frill raised; Finn grins and gives a thumbs up, Zeb copies the proud pose with his chest puffed out.

text: Finn makes a note: horns are for showing
off, and for a push. Case cracked!
p10.prompt: Finn sits on a log writing in his notebook, which shows a simple drawing of two horned dinosaurs pushing with a tick; Zeb sits beside him wearing a pretend set of three twig horns on his hat, both laughing; a Triceratops grazes in the background.

text: On the way back, Zeb spots an old horn
tip in the mud. What should they do?

reveal.text: Today, fossil hunters are asked to leave a special fossil where it is and get help from an expert, so it can be dug out with care. But a horn from long ago could teach us so much! Explorers do not all agree. What would you do?

c2.prompt: On a muddy trail, Zeb crouches and points at an old greyish horn tip sticking out of the mud; Finn kneels beside him with his notebook, thinking hard, chin in hand; the glowing time gate waits far off down the trail.

text: Finn picks up the horn tip. It is heavy!
He wraps it up to take back to the Den.
b2a.prompt: Finn lifts a heavy old horn tip out of the mud with both hands, straining and grinning, while Zeb holds open a cloth bag to wrap it in; muddy prehistoric trail around them.

text: They leave the horn tip in the mud.
One day it may turn into a fossil!
b2b.prompt: Finn and Zeb gently pat mud back over an old horn tip, leaving it where it lies; a little thought bubble above them shows the same horn as a stone fossil being found by a museum scientist far in the future.

text: Zeb holds the book. Finn draws the
horn tip, every bump and crack.
b2c.prompt: Zeb holds Finn's open notebook steady while Finn carefully draws the old horn tip lying in the mud, showing every bump and crack; the drawing on the page is detailed and neat.

text: A storm is coming! Thunder rumbles.
Run for the gate, or shelter and wait?
c3.prompt: Dark storm clouds roll over the prehistoric plain with a flash of lightning far away; the glowing time gate is at the end of a long trail in one direction, and a rocky ledge offers shelter in the other; Finn and Zeb hold their hats as the wind blows, deciding.

text: They dash past the herd in the storm.
The gate hums. In they jump. Zoom!
b3a.prompt: Finn and Zeb run hand in hand through the rain past a calm herd of Triceratops sheltering together, towards the glowing time gate; lightning far away, the boys grinning and splashing through puddles.

text: Under a ledge they wait for the storm
to pass. Then they stroll to the gate.
b3b.prompt: Finn and Zeb sit snug and dry under a rocky ledge while rain pours down in front of them; outside, a Triceratops shelters under a big tree; the storm is starting to clear with a patch of blue sky and a rainbow.

text: Back in the Den, Finn sorts his notes.
Three horns, more to learn. Case cracked!
p11.prompt: Back in the cosy explorer den, Finn pins a drawing of a Triceratops with its three horns onto the corkboard of case notes beside the big fossil horn, while Zeb wears a toy Triceratops hat; the wall screen shows a big green tick.

casefile.title: Triceratops
casefile.subtitle: The name means three-horned face.

facts.text: Triceratops was about 9 metres long. That is as long as a bus.
Each long horn could be about 1 metre long, nearly as long as Finn is tall.
It had up to 160 teeth, about five times as many as a grown-up.

casefile.prompt: A Creature Cases style fact file portrait of a Triceratops, a big gentle plant-eating dinosaur with two long brow horns, a short nose horn, a big bony frill and a parrot-like beak, standing proudly among ferns on a sunny prehistoric plain; clean, bright, centred, like a collector card illustration, no people.

quiz.why: The big one with three horns and a frill.

quiz.q: How many horns did it have?
quiz.why: Two long ones and a short one on its nose.

quiz.q: Why did the two Triceratops push with their horns?

options.text: It was a test of force, not a fight

quiz.why: A pushing contest. Then one got bored and trotted off.

quiz.q: Why might a Triceratops need big horns and a frill?

options.text: To show off and to push

debrief.question: If you had horns like a Triceratops, what would you use them for?
